dimensions.base_interpretation: Realistic is an interest-direction signal about hands-on activity with objects, tools, materials, settings, and visible outputs. It identifies activities worth exploring first in this result; it does not define identity, ability, qualifications, or a career answer.
dimensions.high_reading: If R is relatively high, try small repeatable activities: build or repair something simple; make a rough prototype; or observe a bottleneck in a real process and note its tools, space, and constraints. A higher score only raises exploration priority; it does not prove training, performance, or future outcomes.
dimensions.medium_reading: If R sits in the middle, treat it as a possible side path. Alongside your main interests, try one low-risk hands-on task and notice whether you want to continue, rather than treating it as a long-term direction.
dimensions.low_safe_reading: A lower R score is not a weakness and does not mean you cannot learn or take on related work. It only places these activities lower in this result. When an opportunity matters in real life, use a short task to observe it rather than ruling it out.
dimensions.core_drive: Realistic interest concerns whether activities involving real objects, tools, settings, materials, and visible outputs draw your attention. It is a prompt for exploration, not a statement about personality, capability, eligibility, or the right occupation.
dimensions.possible_cost: Working conditions, physical demands, safety requirements, and training thresholds can shape the experience; an interest score cannot replace those realities.
dimensions.possible_shadow_friction: Job titles can hide important differences in tools, materials, and responsibility. Independent repair, team construction, prototypes, and client-site work may feel very different even when all are hands-on.

dimensions.base_interpretation: Investigative is an interest-direction signal about questions, evidence, mechanisms, variables, and explanatory paths. It identifies activities worth observing in this result; it does not establish research training, ability, or a career conclusion.
dimensions.high_reading: If I is relatively high, try breaking a vague question into hypotheses and variables; compare sources for evidence and uncertainty; or write a possible explanation and list what still needs checking. A higher score only raises exploration priority, not proof of expertise or future results.
dimensions.medium_reading: If I sits in the middle, use it as a possible side path. Try one low-risk inquiry task outside your main interests and notice whether you want to keep investigating, rather than assigning it a permanent role.
dimensions.low_safe_reading: A lower I score is not a deficit and does not mean you cannot learn or complete analytical work. It only places these activities lower in this result. Where they matter, test them through a short task instead of excluding them.
dimensions.core_drive: Investigative interest concerns whether questions, evidence, mechanisms, variables, and explanations invite sustained attention. It is an exploration hypothesis, not evidence of specialist knowledge or a prescribed career.
dimensions.possible_cost: Investigative work can involve slow feedback, incomplete information, and repeated revision; it helps to check whether that pace is workable for you.
dimensions.possible_shadow_friction: Interest in a question does not establish research training, statistical skill, or subject knowledge. Fast decisions or strong social pressure can also obscure how this interest feels in practice.

dimensions.base_interpretation: Artistic is an interest-direction signal about expression, style, narrative, form, and experience. It identifies activities worth exploring in this result; it does not determine creative skill, identity, or occupational fit.
dimensions.high_reading: If A is relatively high, rewrite the same message in two tones; make a rough visual, written, or sound draft; or shape a narrative for one theme and note the pull of the form as well as its pressure. A higher score only raises exploration priority; it does not prove skill or future success.
dimensions.medium_reading: If A sits in the middle, treat it as a possible side path. Try one low-risk expressive task alongside your main interests and see whether you want to return to it, rather than treating it as a fixed direction.
dimensions.low_safe_reading: A lower A score is not a weakness and does not mean you cannot learn or complete expressive work. It only places these activities lower in this result. Where they matter, explore them through a short task instead of rejecting them.
dimensions.core_drive: Artistic interest concerns whether expression, style, narrative, form, and experience invite your attention. It is a prompt to explore activity preferences, not a verdict about talent, training, or a career.
dimensions.possible_cost: Expressive work often includes open standards, revision, and feedback pressure; it helps to check whether those conditions feel workable.
dimensions.possible_shadow_friction: Enjoying expression does not establish creative skill, aesthetic training, or commercial capability. Highly standardized, efficiency-led tasks can also make this interest harder to observe.

dimensions.base_interpretation: Social is an interest-direction signal about people, understanding, support, communication, and collaboration. It identifies activities worth exploring in this result; it does not certify care skills, qualifications, or a career answer.
dimensions.high_reading: If S is relatively high, interview a real need and note both stated and unstated constraints; explain a complex idea to someone and revise your wording; or help with a small task while separating interest in support from the pressure of responsibility. A higher score only raises exploration priority.
dimensions.medium_reading: If S sits in the middle, use it as a possible side path. Try one low-risk collaborative or support task alongside your main interests and notice whether you want to continue, rather than treating it as a fixed direction.
dimensions.low_safe_reading: A lower S score is not a weakness and does not mean you cannot learn or take on people-facing responsibilities. It only places these activities lower in this result. Where they matter, use a short task to observe them instead of ruling them out.
dimensions.core_drive: Social interest concerns whether contact with people, understanding, support, communication, and collaboration draws your attention. It is an exploration prompt, not proof of counselling, education, care, or management competence.
dimensions.possible_cost: People-focused activity can use emotional attention, boundary management, and communication patience; real capacity and context still matter.
dimensions.possible_shadow_friction: Caring about others does not establish professional qualifications. Different people, settings, and levels of responsibility can substantially change the experience of the same support activity.

dimensions.base_interpretation: Enterprising is an interest-direction signal about goals, resources, opportunities, influence, and moving work forward. It identifies activities worth exploring in this result; it does not prove leadership, business judgment, or career suitability.
dimensions.high_reading: If E is relatively high, map stakeholders, resources, and obstacles around a small goal; explain a proposal and notice whether you want to build support; or compare two opportunities by writing their risks, benefits, and assumptions to test. A higher score only raises exploration priority.
dimensions.medium_reading: If E sits in the middle, treat it as a possible side path. Try one low-risk coordination or initiative task outside your main interests and notice whether you want to keep going, rather than treating it as a permanent direction.
dimensions.low_safe_reading: A lower E score is not a weakness and does not mean you cannot learn or take on initiative-related work. It only places these activities lower in this result. Where they matter, test them through a short task instead of excluding them.
dimensions.core_drive: Enterprising interest concerns whether goals, resources, opportunities, influence, and forward movement draw your attention. It is a hypothesis for exploration, not evidence of leadership, commercial ability, or occupational fit.
dimensions.possible_cost: Initiative can involve competition, responsibility, outcome pressure, and incomplete information; it helps to check whether those conditions are workable.
dimensions.possible_shadow_friction: Wanting to influence or organize does not establish leadership, business judgment, or entrepreneurial ability. Unclear goals, authority, or resources can change how this interest feels.

dimensions.base_interpretation: Conventional is an interest-direction signal about rules, data, processes, order, and reviewable records. It identifies activities worth exploring in this result; it does not prove accuracy, qualifications, or a career answer.
dimensions.high_reading: If C is relatively high, organize information into a checklist, table, or reviewable record; inspect a process for omissions, rules, exceptions, and owners; or design a reusable step template and notice whether you want to refine it. A higher score only raises exploration priority.
dimensions.medium_reading: If C sits in the middle, use it as a possible side path. Try one low-risk organization task alongside your main interests and notice whether you want to continue, rather than treating it as a long-term direction.
dimensions.low_safe_reading: A lower C score is not a weakness and does not mean you cannot learn or perform structured work. It only places these activities lower in this result. When they matter, explore them through a short task instead of ruling them out.
dimensions.core_drive: Conventional interest concerns whether rules, data, processes, order, and reviewable records invite your attention. It is a prompt for activity exploration, not proof of accounting, legal, operations, or data-quality ability.
dimensions.possible_cost: Structured work can require patience, detail consistency, and acceptance of rules; actual task intensity still needs checking.
dimensions.possible_shadow_friction: Enjoying order does not establish professional skill. Excessive repetition, unclear authority, or frequently changing standards can change the experience of this kind of activity.
